clue.text: Pastimes I abandoned to become a philosopher

indicators.note: the letter I is abandoned, left out of the word for pastimes

parts.note: pastimes are hobbies

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their leisure pursuits to take up philosophy instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' tells you to drop the I from HOBBIES. Thomas Hobbes was the English philosopher who wrote Leviathan.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hobbes was a seventeenth-century English political thinker, author of Leviathan.

clue.text: What became of Anne Boleyn and Catherine Howard? It's a warning

indicators.note: what happened to these two queens, beheaded, means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: two of Henry VIII's wives, so women

explanation.surface: Asks the fate of two of Henry VIII's executed queens, and calls it a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Both queens were beheaded, so WOMEN lose their heads, the first letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, often a warning of bad luck.

clue.text: Unable to see pen after drinking bout

indicators.note: the word for pen comes after the word for drinking bout

parts.note: a blind is British slang for a drinking spree
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: Someone can no longer see their pen after a heavy session of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is an animal enclosure, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Blindfold as an adjective means with the eyes covered, so not able to see.

clue.text: Poles and European Union not close together

parts.note: spars are poles, as used on a ship's rigging

explanation.surface: Poland and the EU are drifting apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' wants to be people from Poland or the N and S poles; it is SPARS. 'and' and 'Union' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, spread out with gaps between.

clue.text: Classic author of animated character, not altogether superior

indicators.note: the cartoon dog's name is not given in full, losing its final letter

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's cartoon dog
arch- as a prefix means chief or superior, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: A classical writer creates a cartoon figure who is not entirely top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not altogether' cuts the last letter from PLUTO, leaving PLUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch was the Greek biographer of Parallel Lives, a writer from classical antiquity.

clue.text: How to get some fruit juice for meeting with journalists

definitions.text: How to get some fruit juice
definitions.meaning: Conference is a common British variety of pear, so squeezing one yields juice
a briefing at which the media can ask questions

explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a popular British pear variety, so to press one is to get fruit juice.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where a spokesperson takes questions from reporters is a media briefing of this name.

clue.text: Coming nowhere?

parts.note: in a race, finishing outside the first few places means you come nowhere

explanation.definitionFit: A horse that fails to finish in the first three or four positions in a race gets no placing.

clue.text: Did her arrival made Browning homesick?

definitions.text: Did her arrival made Browning homesick?

parts.words: Did her arrival made Browning homesick?
parts.note: Robert Browning's Home-Thoughts, from Abroad begins 'Oh, to be in England now that' a certain spring month is there

explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the year is the springtime that Browning longed to spend in England.

clue.text: Young woman I caught is in court, no romantic

indicators.note: the run of pieces sits inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a lass is a young woman
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman caught in court is said to be quite unsentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the pieces inside the abbreviation for court. Classicism is traditionally set against Romanticism, hence 'no romantic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A classicist favours restraint and classical form, the opposite of the Romantic movement.

clue.text: Something from the past and what woman may not divulge about it

indicators.note: her age goes about, around, the word it

parts.note: a woman may traditionally keep her age secret
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relic from history, and a woman's coy secret about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the woman's secret round the clue's own 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations, a legacy from history.

clue.text: Unpopular type's song with piano hard to follow

indicators.note: hard is placed after the rest, following them

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an aria is an operatic song
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An outcast's song with a piano accompaniment proves hard to keep up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is a social outcast, someone shunned by others.

clue.text: Deprive of official status as one's turned tables in ruin

indicators.note: the anagram goes in the word for ruin

parts.note: to dish someone's hopes is to ruin them
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is the link meaning has

indicators.note: the letters of one plus tables are turned around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone loses official standing after the tables are turned, leaving them ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes ESTABLI from one and tables; 'in' sets it inside the word for ruin. 'As' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To disestablish is to strip something, often a state church, of its official standing.

clue.text: See a man struggling with a tentacled marine creature

indicators.note: the letters of the three words struggle into a new arrangement

parts.note: a means one, a single thing

explanation.surface: A swimmer sees a man wrestling with a sea creature that has tentacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges SEE A MAN into SEAANEM; the second 'a' gives ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea anemone is a soft-bodied sea animal with a ring of stinging tentacles.

clue.text: Priestess's object of worship

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth, the priestess of Aphrodite at Sestos whom Leander swam to see
an idol, someone admired and looked up to

explanation.definitionFit: Hero is the mythical priestess loved by Leander, and a hero is an idolised figure.

clue.text: Excessive number of deliveries to miller's boy

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
Much the Miller's Son is one of Robin Hood's Merry Men

explanation.surface: Too many deliveries are being made to the miller's son.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is six deliveries from one bowler. In the Robin Hood stories, Much is the miller's son.
explanation.definitionFit: Overmuch means too much, beyond what is reasonable, so it is a synonym for excessive.

clue.text: Exploits with fish in the drink

parts.note: to milk someone is to exploit them
hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone does daring deeds with fish in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like a noun, heroic deeds, but it is a verb: MILKS. 'in the drink' suggests the sea; only 'drink' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkshake is a sweet cold beverage of milk whisked with flavouring.

clue.text: Rub us the wrong way with prejudice, mostly in places like Harrow

indicators.note: rubbing the wrong way shuffles the two words into a new order
most of the word for prejudice is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: bias is prejudice

explanation.surface: Snobbish places like Harrow irritate us with their prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' rearranges RUB US into SUBUR, and 'mostly' trims BIAS to BIA. Harrow is a London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburbia is the collective term for suburbs such as Harrow on the edge of London.

clue.text: Restrain worker leading strike

indicators.note: the word for worker comes first, at the head of the other piece

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the hand

explanation.surface: The bosses hold back a worker who leads a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' is a hit here, not a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff someone is to restrain them by shackling their wrists.

clue.text: Tie up and whip

definitions.meaning: a stroke of a whip, or to flog

explanation.definitionFit: To lash is both to bind with cord and to flog with a whip.

clue.text: Gift of finest old whiskey

parts.note: best means finest
Whiskey is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for W

explanation.surface: A present of the best aged whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gift' is a verb here, to give. Whiskey stands for W in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To gift something is to bestow it, to give it as a present.

clue.text: Where top brass are taking sovereign's side, without mercy

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the coin side goes round mercy

parts.note: the side of a coin bearing the monarch's head is heads
to give no quarter is to show no mercy

explanation.surface: Officers seize the monarch's faction and show no clemency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, so the coin side goes round mercy. A sovereign is also a British gold coin. 'taking' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Headquarters is the base from which senior commanders direct operations.

clue.text: Had a meal — bought it about noon

indicators.note: the word for died goes round the letter for noon

parts.note: bought it is slang for died

explanation.surface: Someone ate, after buying lunch at around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bought it' is slang for died, not a purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a main meal, so had a meal is the past tense.

clue.text: Novelist said what kind of person he was

definitions.text: what kind of person he was

indicators.note: the novelist's name as spoken, which sounds the same

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott, author of Ivanhoe

explanation.surface: A novelist declares his own nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Scott was born in Edinburgh, so he was Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott was a native of Scotland, so his nationality is the word sounded.

clue.text: Mix socially in jobs newly started

indicators.note: the first job is made anew, given a fresh letter in place of its J

parts.note: two jobs give two copies of the word job

indicators.note: the second job is started differently, its J swapped for another letter

parts.note: the second job

explanation.surface: Someone networks at events while settling into new posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly started' means each JOB gets a new first letter: H in one, N in the other. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mingle socially, especially with people of higher standing.

clue.text: Bird included in menu that chef put together

indicators.note: the bird is contained within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A bird appears on the menu that the chef put together.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is hidden across meNU THAT CHef. 'put together' tells you to read the three words joined up.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small tree-climbing songbird.

clue.text: Person who's crazy, in a nutshell?

definitions.meaning: a mad or unbalanced person, in slang
nut is slang for head, so a nutshell is the case round the head

explanation.walkthrough: A head case is slang for a crazy person; read as two words it is the case that holds a head, a 'nut' in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Headcase is British slang for someone mad or unpredictable, a nutter.

clue.text: Memorial recollecting the war

indicators.note: collecting the letters again, re-collecting them into a new order

explanation.surface: A memorial that brings back memories of the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' read as re-collecting rearranges THE WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of flowers is laid at a memorial, as on Remembrance Day.
